hyperedges.label: graphify Build Pipeline (Detect → Extract → Build → Label → Export)

nodes.label: Post-Commit Hook (Amp)
nodes.rationale: No background process needed - triggers once per commit, works with any editor; appends to an existing post-commit hook rather than replacing it

nodes.label: graphify amp install
nodes.rationale: Run once per project so graphify is always-on in Amp sessions without a manual /graphify

nodes.label: Post-Commit Hook (Claude Code)
nodes.rationale: Doc/image changes are ignored by the hook because only AST re-extraction is cheap enough per commit; those need a manual /graphify --update

nodes.label: Trae Lacks PreToolUse Hooks
nodes.rationale: Unlike Claude Code, Trae does not support PreToolUse hooks, so AGENTS.md rules are the only always-on mechanism and graph refresh must be run manually

nodes.label: Extraction Subagent Prompt (Compact)
nodes.rationale: Loaded only when the corpus has at least one doc, paper, or image; a pure-code corpus skips Part B and never reads it

nodes.label: Deterministic Node ID Format
nodes.rationale: IDs must match the AST extractor's ID and stay deterministic from the label alone, so chunk or sequence suffixes are forbidden

nodes.label: Confidence Score Rubric
nodes.rationale: 0.5 is banned as a default so scores carry real signal; if no bucket fits, the edge is marked AMBIGUOUS instead

nodes.label: Verbatim source_file Rule
nodes.rationale: Keeps full build and --update on one base so build_merge's replace matches instead of duplicating nodes

nodes.label: DEEP_MODE Extraction
nodes.rationale: Be aggressive with INFERRED edges for indirect deps and latent couplings; mark uncertain ones AMBIGUOUS instead of omitting

nodes.label: semantically_similar_to Edge Rule
nodes.rationale: Captures concepts that solve the same problem when no import, call, or citation links them structurally

nodes.label: Hyperedge Rule (Max 3 Per Chunk)
nodes.rationale: Only when 3+ nodes share a concept not captured by pairwise edges, so hyperedges stay informative

nodes.label: Six-Value file_type Enum
nodes.rationale: Any value outside code, document, paper, image, rationale, concept is invalid and rejected

nodes.label: Fast Path for Existing Graph
nodes.rationale: If graph.json already exists and the user asks a codebase question, skip Steps 1-5 and query directly — the graph is already built, rebuilding wastes tokens

nodes.label: Step 0 - GitHub Clone and Multi-Path Merge
Step 2 - Detect Files
nodes.rationale: Sidecar is written from Python rather than a shell redirect so the same block renders on PowerShell hosts without console-encoding drift (#2528)

nodes.label: Corpus Size Warning and Narrowing
nodes.rationale: Above 2M words or 500 files, ask the user to narrow to a subfolder; skipped_sensitive files are listed so a wrongly-flagged source is visible and can be renamed (#2106)

nodes.label: Step 3 - Extract Entities and Relationships
nodes.rationale: Part A (AST) and Part B (semantic) run in parallel because they operate on different file types, saving 5-15s on large corpora

nodes.label: No API Key Required Policy
nodes.rationale: Code is extracted structurally with no LLM; graphify never reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY, and prompting for one is a misread of the skill

nodes.label: Gemini Semantic Extraction Backend
nodes.rationale: Used only when GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY is already set; otherwise the host agent itself is the LLM

nodes.label: Part A - Structural AST Extraction
nodes.rationale: Deterministic and free — no LLM and no key at all

nodes.label: Part B - Semantic Extraction via Subagents
nodes.rationale: Uses the Agent tool because reading files one-by-one is 5-10x slower; a code-only corpus writes an empty semantic file so Part C's unconditional read does not hit FileNotFoundError

nodes.label: Step B0 - Check Extraction Cache
nodes.rationale: Cache entries are attributed to SPEC_PATH so a changed extraction prompt forces re-extraction while unchanged prompts keep their entries (#1939); only content files go to semantic extraction since code is covered by AST (#1392)

nodes.label: Step B1 - Split Into Chunks
nodes.rationale: Each image gets its own chunk because vision needs separate context; same-directory files are grouped so cross-file relationships are more likely to be extracted

nodes.label: Step B3 - Collect, Cache, and Merge Chunks
nodes.rationale: Chunk file existence on disk is the success signal; a missing file means the subagent was likely read-only and must be surfaced rather than silently skipped

nodes.label: Part C - Merge AST + Semantic
nodes.rationale: AST nodes go first and semantic nodes are deduplicated by id, so structural extraction wins on conflict

nodes.label: Step 4 - Build, Cluster, Analyze, Output
nodes.rationale: root= mirrors the --update runbook (#1361) so full build and incremental update never drift apart on re-extract

nodes.label: Empty Extraction Guard
nodes.rationale: Checked immediately after build and before any write so an empty extraction cannot clobber a good graph.json, GRAPH_REPORT.md, or analysis sidecar (#1392)

nodes.label: graph.json Shrink Guard (#479)
nodes.rationale: to_json returns False when the new graph is smaller than the existing one; the report and analysis sidecar are only written after a successful export so they never describe a graph graph.json does not contain (#1392)

nodes.label: Step 4.5 - Graph Health Check
nodes.rationale: Read-only and never aborts — it surfaces edge collapse, dangling/missing endpoints, and self-loops, the silent-corruption modes of incremental updates and AST/LLM id mismatches

nodes.label: Step 5 - Label Communities
nodes.rationale: Questions are regenerated with real labels because labels affect question phrasing; graph.json is re-exported so nodes carry the curated community_name (#2490)

nodes.label: Step 6 - Obsidian Vault and HTML Export
nodes.rationale: Obsidian is opt-in because it generates one file per node; HTML is always generated unless --no-viz

nodes.label: Step 9 - Manifest, Cost Tracker, Cleanup
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files that actually produced output are stamped so a failed chunk stays unstamped and is re-queued rather than lost forever (#2015); stale semantic hashes are cleared (#1948) and the raw corpus is used as scan_corpus so newly excluded files are dropped, not read as deletions (#1908)

nodes.label: Interpreter Guard for Subcommands
nodes.rationale: Re-resolves the interpreter when .graphify_python is missing, e.g. after the user deleted graphify-out/

nodes.label: Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge, never hide cohesion behind symbols, always show token cost — the audit trail is only useful if it is honest

nodes.label: Step B2 Dispatch - Agent Tool (Disk)
nodes.rationale: All Agent calls must be in the same response — sequential calls defeat parallelism

nodes.label: general-purpose Subagent Type Requirement
nodes.rationale: Explore is read-only and cannot write chunk files to disk, which silently drops extraction results; general-purpose has the Write and Bash access the subagent needs

nodes.label: Absolute CHUNK_PATH Derivation
nodes.rationale: PROJECT_ROOT must be cwd, where Part C globs graphify-out/, not the .graphify_root scan dir (#1392)

nodes.label: Step B2 Dispatch - Codex spawn_agent
nodes.rationale: Codex collects results in memory, so there are no per-chunk files on disk and Step B3's disk success checks do not apply — invalid JSON is the failure signal instead; requires multi_agent = true in ~/.codex/config.toml

nodes.label: Step B2 Dispatch - Manual Paste
nodes.rationale: This host has no parallel Agent/Task API, so extraction is driven by hand and each response is written to its own chunk file before Step B3 runs

nodes.label: Step B2 Dispatch - OpenCode @mention
nodes.rationale: All mentions in a single message run in parallel; falls back to the serial chunk-file path if @agent cannot write to disk

nodes.label: Step B2 Dispatch - Task Tool (Trae)
nodes.rationale: Trae does not support PreToolUse hooks, so AGENTS.md rules are the always-on mechanism instead

nodes.label: Kilo-Specific Rules
nodes.rationale: Kilo uses subagent_type="general" and launches all chunk tasks in one response so they run in parallel

nodes.label: PowerShell 5.1 Scrolling Breakage
nodes.rationale: Caused by ANSI escape sequences emitted by the graspologic library; uninstalling it falls back to NetworkX Louvain, which produces no ANSI output

nodes.label: graphify query Flow
nodes.rationale: When graph.json exists, answer from the graph rather than rebuilding it

nodes.label: Question Vocabulary Expansion
nodes.rationale: Expand the question against the graph's own vocabulary before traversal so a wording mismatch does not collapse the answer to noise

nodes.label: AGENTS.md Hooks Reference Template
nodes.rationale: Placeholder-driven template so each host's hooks reference is generated from one source

nodes.label: PowerShell Interpreter Guard
nodes.rationale: The interpreter that owns the graphify entry point sits next to it (<env>\Scripts\python.exe for uv tool, pipx, and venv installs)

nodes.label: POSIX Install and Interpreter Detection
nodes.rationale: Tries uv tool first (most reliable on modern Mac/Linux), then the graphify shebang for pipx/pip installs, then python3; writes the interpreter path so it persists across invocations

nodes.label: PowerShell Install and Interpreter Detection
nodes.rationale: uv/pipx-aware detection (fixes #831); 'uv tool dir' and 'pipx environment' are authoritative and respect UV_TOOL_DIR/PIPX_HOME automatically

nodes.label: .graphify_root Scan Root Sidecar
nodes.rationale: Saved so `graphify update` with no args knows where to look next time

nodes.label: Reproducible Example Walkthrough
nodes.rationale: Seven files, two languages, no PDF or image extraction — runs entirely on AST and markdown with no token cost for semantic extraction

nodes.label: Document Pipeline Architecture
nodes.rationale: The pipeline is intentionally linear with no event bus or dependency injection, which makes the call graph easy to follow and easy to test

nodes.label: Parsing Stage
nodes.rationale: Each format is handled differently; new formats are added as a branch in parse_file plus a new parse_* function so the rest of the pipeline does not change

nodes.label: Storage Stage
nodes.rationale: All modules read and write through the storage interface so there is one source of truth; a flat JSON index plus one file per document is enough at small scale but becomes the bottleneck past a few thousand documents

nodes.label: Cross-Reference Detection
nodes.rationale: Intentionally naive — keyword overlap of three is reasonable for short documents but produces too many false positives on long ones; a real system would use TF-IDF or embedding similarity

nodes.label: Keyword Extraction Approach
nodes.rationale: Strips stopwords and returns unique tokens — simple, fast, and debuggable, but treats all keywords equally regardless of position

nodes.label: TF-IDF Weighting
nodes.rationale: Gives higher scores to words distinctive to a document; worth switching once the index has ~50+ documents so IDF is meaningful

nodes.label: Embedding-Based Similarity
nodes.rationale: Much better recall but adds a dependency and makes the index opaque

nodes.label: Flat Files vs SQLite
nodes.rationale: Flat files are easy to inspect with no tooling, which matters for debugging; SQLite becomes worth it for range queries or field-level updates without rewriting the whole record

nodes.label: API Layer Transaction Risk
nodes.rationale: parse_and_save calls validate_document then save_parsed in sequence; a save failure after successful validation leaves a partially written record — fine at small scale, a problem under load

nodes.label: Storage Interface Abstraction Question
nodes.rationale: A repository pattern would centralize access but adds indirection — probably not worth it until the storage backend needs to change

nodes.label: httpx Graph Report
nodes.rationale: 144 nodes, 330 edges, 6 communities; 53% EXTRACTED / 47% INFERRED at zero token cost

nodes.label: Client (god node)
nodes.rationale: Highest-degree node at 26 edges and a cross-community bridge (betweenness 0.177)

nodes.label: Surprising Connections Section
nodes.rationale: Surfaces INFERRED cross-file links (e.g. Timeout uses URL/Headers/Cookies) the reader would not think to ask about

nodes.label: Suggested Questions Section
nodes.rationale: Built from betweenness centrality bridges and high-INFERRED-degree nodes that need verification
